findings.message: evals/runner.py:1569-1637 and :1721-1730. GRADERS G-05 has applies_to ['BLK_02'], but its rubric declares RUB-EC-08, -16, -17, -24 and -25 for BLK_01 and RUB-EC-01 for a BLK_01 case. evaluate() never checks applies_to or the payload's agent, so it sends any payload it gets to the judge. This contradiction in the Precord is a compiler-style finding (COMPILER_FINDING): it should be recorded as a gap or deviation, but none of scope.recorded_gaps mentions it. Record it. Do not decide which side is right in the code.

evals/runner.py:1656 and :1725-1726. evaluate() returns {'check': 'G-02', 'passed': False} for a non-dict or empty-dict payload. G-02's declared criterion is 'Output validates against the agent's out.schema.json'. The recorded gap says those schemas declare no properties, so an empty object passes the real G-02, and the harness has already run G-02 before it calls evaluate. Reporting G-02 as the grader that decided the case mislabels a check that the runner made up and that graders.yaml does not define. Only a non-dict payload is a real schema failure. An empty dict should go to the judge, or the result should not carry the G-02 ID.

evals/runner.py:1745-1746. verdict() drops every passing result, including monitor-tier ones. Rule 6 of the eval-compilation skill says 'Record a monitor result', and rule 7 says to report the achieved value of a monitor metric without pass or fail. With this code, a passing monitor metric such as tokens_per_case does not appear anywhere in the verdict. The component instructions only require misses in 'recorded', so this is a gap in the skill obligation, not a contract break.

evals/runner.py:1712-1718. _judged_pass() passes only when the first line is exactly the token PASS once the surrounding punctuation is stripped. A common one-line judge reply such as 'PASS: meets the rubric' or 'PASS - ...' becomes 'PASS: MEETS THE RUBRIC' and is scored as a fail. That produces silent false negatives in the repair loop. Use the first word of the first line instead.

evals/runner.py:1688-1689 and :1742. tier_of() raises ValueError when tier_at_rung is not monitor, advisory or blocking, and verdict() calls it without a guard. If a caller passes thresholds with a blank or unexpected tier, the whole verdict aborts instead of the result being recorded. The pinned THRESHOLDS are all valid today, so this only affects caller-supplied thresholds.
